name: Florida Power & Light

summary.text: Florida Power & Light (FPL), a subsidiary of NextEra Energy, is Florida's largest electric utility. Reporting by the Orlando Sentinel, Miami Herald and Floodlight from 2021 tied consultants who worked for FPL, at Matrix LLC, to Florida's 2020 'ghost candidate' campaigns; a 2019 email from CEO Eric Silagy directed staff to make state Sen. José Javier Rodríguez's life 'a living hell'. FPL and NextEra denied wrongdoing, said outside law firms cleared the company, and Silagy retired in January 2023. The FEC deadlocked 3-3 on a related complaint in 2024.

facts.claim: FPL's then-CEO Eric Silagy acknowledged writing a January 2019 email directing subordinates to make Sen. José Javier Rodríguez's life 'a living hell'; he called it a poor choice of words and denied directing Matrix to do anything illegal.
facts.quote: Silagy has called his wording a "poor choice of words" but has denied that he or the company directed Matrix to do anything illegal.

Records show senior Florida Power & Light execs closely connected to election scandals

facts.claim: In the 2020 race, a no-party 'ghost' candidate named Alex Rodriguez drew more than 6,000 votes and incumbent José Javier Rodríguez lost by 32 votes; leaked Matrix documents tied Matrix employees to ads for the ghost candidate.
facts.quote: Garcia barely eked out a victory, besting José Javier Rodríguez by a scant 32 votes.

facts.claim: No one from FPL or Matrix has been charged; FPL has repeatedly denied the allegations, and NextEra said in an SEC filing that its investigation was substantially complete and FPL would likely not be found liable for Florida campaign-finance violations.
facts.quote: In a SEC filing, NextEra said its investigation "is substantially complete" and that FPL would likely not be found liable for Florida campaign finance violations.

facts.claim: FPL says two outside law firms it commissioned cleared it of election-related liability; the reviews have not been made public.
facts.quote: The utility claims that two outside law firms, whose investigations FPL commissioned but has never made public, have cleared it of election-related liability or wrongdoing.

facts.claim: The FEC deadlocked 3-3 in February 2024 on CREW's complaint that FPL used Matrix-linked nonprofits to hide political spending and closed the file; NextEra said it was told the file was closed.
facts.quote: NextEra Energy, FPL's parent, said it was told the FEC voted to close the file.

facts.claim: Former state senator Frank Artiles was convicted on September 30, 2024 on three election charges for paying ghost candidate Alex Rodriguez $44,000 and was sentenced to 60 days in jail plus probation.
facts.quote: He was convicted on three election-related charges for his work running the campaign of Alex Rodriguez

connections.quote: Jeff Pitts, then at Matrix, sent FPL's then-CEO Eric Silagy two memos in November 2019.
